equivalents.note: The Tibetan does not transcribe the rāga name but calls the melody glu dbyangs chen po, 'the great melody', so chen po stands where the Bengali has gauṛā.

rigs skye ba renders kula-jana, 'people of family', with nothing for 'good'; with the preceding mtha' (for ante) it can also be read as mtha' rigs, 'border or outcaste lineage', which would reverse the sense, so the division is unclear.
The Tibetan has 'people of good family' rather than 'the wise', as if reading a word like kulīna, echoing rigs skye ba for kuliṇajaṇa in 2b.
Where the Bengali names Ḍombī, the Tibetan has gdol pa mo, its ordinary word for a caṇḍāla woman, so the line reads 'there is no low-caste woman beyond the caṇḍāla woman'.
The Tibetan has dmangs rigs, 'low caste' (śūdra), a caste term rather than a word for an unchaste woman.

The Tibetan breaks up the compound, making the yogin the one who falls asleep (rol rtsed kyis rnal 'byor pa gnyid du song ba, 'through play the yogin went to sleep') instead of naming a yogic sleep (rnal 'byor gyi gnyid).
Here the first element is transcribed d+hU, without the r of dhru- (elsewhere d+h+rU'i rkang pa or brtan pa'i rkang pa).

The Tibetan transcribes ka pA la, which keeps Munidatta's etymology of ka (conventional bodhicitta) and pāla (protecting), and the segment breaks off right after it, with nothing for cittavajra-ādhānaṃ.
caryāpādāḥ, introducing the quotation, is rendered glu dbyangs zhabs, 'the master of song', so caryā is taken as the songs rather than as conduct.
asampradāya- 'without the lineage' is rendered man ngag dang bral ba'i, 'lacking instruction', so sampradāya is read as instruction (man ngag), as in bla ma'i man ngag elsewhere.

For asampradāyayoginyā, the yoginī of one without the lineage, the Tibetan has a male yogin (man ngag dang bral ba'i rnal 'byor pas), making the uninstructed practitioner, not Ḍombī as yoginī, the one who destroys the moon.
The Tibetan transcribes the code word as po la (dga' ba'i po la, 'dear bola'), as it does kakkola (kak+ko la), and does not translate it.
The Tibetan renders kāliñjarāḥ by sense as skal ba dang ldan, 'fortunate', instead of transcribing it (kA liM dza ra) as it does in the Hevajra quotation on song 4.
'gul ba ('to move, shake') stands where the Sanskrit has kaṇṭhe, apparently a slip for mgul ba 'neck', the word the Tibetan uses for kaṇṭha in 4b.
pretāvāsanivāsa is rendered dur khrod gnas su gnas par, 'dwelling in the place of the charnel ground', with nivāsa as the verb gnas pa and the abode of the dead as a charnel ground.
In the next sentence svarūpānabhijñāḥ, 'not knowing the true nature', appears as rang bzhin gyis mngon par shes pa, with no negative.
Here the Tibetan has plain bsngags pa, 'praise', not rjes su bsngags pa as elsewhere.

The Tibetan does not translate chinnanāsikā, 'a woman whose nose is cut off', but repeats dmangs rigs from the song line, and then says a town woman (grong khyer ma nyid yod pa'o) does exist, where the Sanskrit denies both.

equivalents.lemma: ngo bo nyid mi gnas pa
equivalents.note: In a garbled rendering of the verse, niḥsvabhāvatā becomes ngo bo nyid mi gnas pa, 'the essence does not abide', construed with nirvāṇa, not the expected rang bzhin med pa.

questions: dombi in cp.18.3a: the Tibetan line (kye ma khyod ni rnam par nyams byed de) does not name Ḍombī; it addresses her only as khyod 'you' after kye ma, and has nothing for saala 'all'. So there is no equivalent to give for this line. The commentary (cp.18.m4) does have Dom+bi ni for her.

p-virupa in cp.18.4a: this is a false match. Here biruā means 'ill, wrongly' (kehe keho tohore biruā bolai, 'some speak ill of you'), not the poet Virūpa. Munidatta glosses it viruddhaṃ vadanti (cp.18.m5), and the Tibetan has ngan par brjod, 'speak badly' (in m5, 'gal bar smra ba). I have given no equivalent. Should the বিরুআ form be kept off p-virupa, or a separate word entry be made?

trivajra (cittavajra) in cp.18.m3: the Tibetan segment breaks off at 'ka pA la ni', so kāpālikaś cittavajra-ādhānaṃ kṛtam has no Tibetan here and no equivalent can be given. The rest of the sentence may be lost or misaligned.

pada in cp.18.m4: the Tibetan of m4 starts at the comment on 3a (de yis Dom+bi ni…) and has nothing for the opening viśiṣya padāntareṇa tām evoparāgayati — tam̐i lo ityādi, so padāntareṇa has no equivalent here. rkang pa for pada is already matched in m5 and m6.
